NEWEST WAY TO FIGHT FIRES. PORTAELE PHONE FOR FIRE FIGHTING.

By means of a portable telephone device a fire chief can now send his commands by phone to firemen within a burning building, greatly reducing risk of life, according to official tests recently made by Fire Chief Thomas R. Murphy of San Francisco. Firemen are equipped with a receiver kit which can be instantly attack to a special wire and the commanding officer can attend restrictions. Messengers have heretofore been used and delays are frequent.

Masks that are to supply oxygen to firemen
riding their lives and smoke and suffocating
fuses must be absolutely leakproof. Therefore
weekly inspection of masks is a part of the
routine of every fire company.

One man does the mask and another coats all the seams and joints with compounds using a shaving brush for this purpose. The artificial air supply is then turned on and the inspector carefully looks for any tiny soap bubbles indicating leaks. All defective masks are at once marked and repaired

After the soap lids test the firemen with mask well fastened enters a sealed room with turning formaldehyde giving off poisonous gases. If the firemen can remain in the room for fifteen minutes without giddiness or any sense of suffocation it is positive proof that the mask is functioning properly

LONDON'S LATEST FIRE ENGINE.

Londons latest fire fighters are the most remarkable engines, in the country, they have been devised for the purpose of dealing with blazing oil or petrol when the use of ordinary engine pumps are useless. The new engine is composed of a large tank containing two liquids which when formed together makes a thick foam.
0.P.S. The "stost fire fighter."
NEW MOTOR TURNABLE FIRE ESCAPE.

This is the first machine of its type ever constructed in this country or elsewhere. The ladder is operated upon a special hydraulic system. It is carried on a 65 horse-power motor chassis of the standard type, and when fully extended will reach a height of eighty-five feet for use as a fire escape or water tower. The hydraulic pressure for raising, extending, and revolving the ladder on the turntable is provided by a three throw pump fixed at the rear of the framing and driven through a reduction gear from the engine shaft in the change gear box. The pump delivers oil under pressure to three different machines. The ladder can be raised and extended in less than a minute and operations of extending and slewing can be performed simultaneously.

NEW LOUD-SPEAKER FIRE ALARM.

A new type of street fire-alarm which is like a loud speaker is being installed in Birmingham and experiments have shown that valuable time is saved by its use. When the glass panels is broken the door immediately swings open and the person giving the alarm simply speaks into a horn. His voice is amplified at the other end and the firemen on duty we at once informed of the outbreak.

O.P.S. The new loud-speaker Fire Alarm being installed in street of Birmingham.

The inauguration of New York City's new fire alarm telegraph system was held today, at the Fire Alarm Central Office,79th Street, Central Park. This station receives all fire alarms turned in throut the city, and relays them to nearest station from where the alarm has been turned. The station has 217 working box circuits, 350 miles of cable and 17,000 miles of wire in its mechanism. The station cost $1,500,000 and required ten years to complete. A call can be telegraphed any where in the city within ten seconds. The system works, as follows: A call comes in on the relay board, the number of the district recording, being heard by the operator, seen by the operator and registering itself to prevent any error. To call an engine company, a metal perforated disk is inserted into the selective switch machine, each company having separate disks, which transmits the number to the transmitting machine, from which machine the various companies receive instructions as to location of fire, etc. 6/29/22

Four big gray ships, built by the government-during the war at a cost of nearly four million dollars, were set on fire last week on the beach of the Columbia River, Portland, Oregon, where they have laid for the last several months. They were purchased some time ago by a western syndicate for $4000, and after the hardware had been removed, the boat were fired.

HEAVY LOSS IN DOCKS WAREHOUSE BLAZE.

The ruins of a large warehouse which was the scene of a fierce fire at Middlesborough Docks yesterday. Damage estimated at £30,000 was done and two liners were scorched by the flames. Trucks with goods were destroyed. Mar 24th.
